Hi Lauren / Daniel —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Per our discussion, attaching a working Mutual Action Plan and an initial evaluation checklist so we can align on acceptance gates for the activation milestone. High-level asks here:

- We will run a focused performance sweep that measures: time-to-first-token (TTFT, defined below), streaming head latency (first-stream-byte latency), p50/p95/p99 for both, and concurrency behavior across a staircase (1, 5, 20, 50 concurrent users).
- Acceptance criteria (proposed): TTFT p95 <= 350ms on your representative prompts; streaming head p95 <= 120ms; end-to-end token throughput >= 18 tokens/sec at 20 concurrent users for baseline model.
- Redwood will run the bench in our staging region on a dedicated pool and share raw logs and a short summary (CSV + latency plots).

Attached: healthsync_map_v2.xlsx (MAP with milestones, owners, deadlines). Please review the timeline column — we propose a 7-business-day evaluation window starting the week of 2028-04-15.

Aditya — can you own the bench plan + test harness? Vanessa and I will coordinate the MAP updates and procurement questions.

Next steps: Lauren, confirm the representative prompt set and whether you want tokenization-normalized metrics (we can normalize by subtoken tokens if helpful). Also confirm procurement contact for PO cadence (cc'd procurement@healthsync.ai if different).

Cheers,
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: HealthSync MAP — activation eval & streaming latency readout

Connor / Lauren / Vanessa —

I put together the benchmarking protocol and a quick harness plan. Key points:

1) Definitions (explicit):
   - Time-to-first-token (TTFT): measured at Redwood edge ingress timestamp T0 to first-stream-byte emitted from model runtime T1. TTFT = T1 - T0. We will provide both edge-to-first-byte and gateway-to-first-byte so you can compare.
   - Streaming head latency: for long-form streaming, we additionally measure first-stream-chunk latency (first 32-token chunk) as a separate metric.

2) Staircase concurrency: runs at concurrency levels [1, 5, 10, 20, 50]. Each run = 500 requests per concurrency level; inter-arrival jitter added to mimic bursty UAT traffic.

3) p50/p95/p99 reporting: we will report sample percentiles and include raw histograms. We'll also include per-request token counts and token-RT profiles.

4) Environment and model variant: staging cluster in us-west-2, dedicated pool m60x2 (quantized model variant q4_0) + fallback to fp16 variant if we see >10% error rates.

5) Artifacts we will deliver: bench-log-20280413.csv (raw request log), screenshot-latency-plot.png (latency curves), short notes on anomalies.

Preliminary finding from today's quick run (single-shot): TTFT p50=210ms, p95=360ms, p99=490ms; streaming head p50=90ms, p95=140ms, p99=250ms. These are from a first pass with the longer dialog prompts mixed in — I will run the full staircase tomorrow and post updated CSV.

Open questions for HealthSync:
- Do you want tokenization-normalized TTFT (tokens per second) or raw TTFT in ms? We can provide both.
- Is the staged pool acceptable, or do you want us to run on a dedicated Cluster ID you manage?

Will follow up with full staircase results.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
SRE, Performance | Redwood Inference

Team — thank you for the fast turnaround. We reviewed the stair-step results and artifacts. Summary from our side:

- We reviewed bench-log-20280413.csv and screenshot-latency-plot.png. The full staircase posted by Aditya (staircase run id: hs-stair-0416) shows: TTFT p50=220ms, p95=380ms, p99=520ms; streaming head p50=95ms, p95=130ms, p99=230ms at concurrency=20.
- These meet our acceptance gate (p95 TTFT <= 400ms). We have a minor UX flag around p99 spikes on a particular long-dialog prompt (ID L-17) — we've attached examples in the Drive folder.

Decision: Accept the activation evaluation. Proceed to canary rollout (2028-04-25) with a 24-hour monitoring window and rollback policy as defined in the MAP. Procurement: please send PO instructions and invoice template to procurement@healthsync.ai; PO expected ~3 weeks.

Thanks everyone — Connor / Vanessa, please confirm canary run cadence and that Redwood will share hourly latency dashboards during the 24-hour window.

Best,
Lauren
